findings.title: A proven-fake assertion: the overflow log line cap value is asserted by the wall clock
findings.reason: toContain(String(cap)) over the JSON-stringified console.warn call is satisfied by the logger own ISO timestamp. The identical mutant (cap: 0) was killed at 07:37:0x and survived on a re-run at another instant, so the oracle is the system clock. The log line EXISTENCE has a real oracle (toHaveLength(1) kills M13); its payload has none. Replacement: JSON.parse the line and toMatchObject({ cap, flag }).

findings.title: Runbook: "Rule 6 is the one still genuinely owed" is false at HEAD and contradicted eleven lines below by the same commit
findings.reason: This branch added rules 7 and 8 and, at line 383 of the same file in the same commit, recorded that both also have no rule in either project. Three rules are owed at HEAD, not one. The edit that changed the register left the ownership sentence stale.

findings.title: The overflow marker fires on ONE distinct code when a call carries duplicates, and permanently burns the paging latch
findings.reason: overflowed = fresh.length > room compares ARRAY ENTRIES against SET SLOTS, and fresh is deliberately not de-duplicated. Reproduced with a journaled probe: nine copies of one unmapped code emit both the report (naming the code eight times) and auto_approval_unmapped_block_reason_cap_reached (runbook rule 8, a first-seen error page documented as ">CAP DISTINCT codes"), and the once-per-process latch then suppresses the genuine cap-reached page (probe measured 0 captures at the real cap). Not reachable from the sole production caller today because compactBlockReasons de-duplicates, which is why this is P1; the module docblock and docs/directory.md both declare duplicate input supported and meaningful. One-line fix: de-duplicate fresh, or compare new Set(fresh).size > room.

findings.title: The Set-bound half of the round-2 fix has no oracle
findings.reason: Mutant M5 restores exactly the round-2 P0 (add every fresh code rather than only the reported ones) and survives 31/31 with no other covering test. Four documents assert the bound; the branch own new test comment concedes the gap ("If the Set had grown past cap this would still pass"). Minimal fix: a test-only size reader beside resetUnmappedBlockReasonSignalForTests, asserted toBe(cap) after the cap+3 call.

findings.title: The un-ruled-signal register applies a warning-level premise to two error-level signals
findings.reason: The register lists both new error-level fault signals as having no rule in either project, but its own rule-6 reasoning six lines above is that a WARNING captureMessage does not classify as high priority and therefore escapes the unfiltered production rule 3920752 - which implies an ERROR capture does not escape it. Either the two new signals are already routed by 3920752 or the rule-6 premise is wrong. Needs a Sentry read-back, not a guess.
